title: Master the Art of Timing
coreMove: Wait for ripeness and move when timing makes the same action easier to accept
sourcePressure: Chapter 35 centers on timing as a decisive part of power. The law values patience, rhythm, and recognition of ripeness because the same move can fail when launched too early or too late and succeed when it meets the field at the right moment. Its limit is that timing judgment collapses when it becomes superstition, passive drift, or endless delay disguised as wisdom. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
